expo.name: GoalSlot
expo.description: GoalSlot turns your goals into a schedule you actually follow — plan your day, track tasks, and time your focus sessions, online or off.

android._permissionsComment: What makes a schedule reminder land ON the minute. expo-notifications picks its AlarmManager method at runtime: `if (SDK_INT < S || canScheduleExactAlarms()) setExactAndAllowWhileIdle(...) else setAndAllowWhileIdle(...)`. Without these, that check fails on Android 12+ and every reminder degrades to the INEXACT branch, which Doze can defer by many minutes — a 9:00 block announcing itself at 9:20. SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM covers API 31-32; USE_EXACT_ALARM covers API 33+ and is required on Android 14+, where the former is no longer auto-granted. PLAY POLICY: USE_EXACT_ALARM is restricted to apps whose core function is an alarm clock or calendar — confirm before the next Play submission. Dropping it still leaves exact alarms working on Android 12-13.

plugins._comment: NON-FUNCTIONAL PLACEHOLDER. No `organization`/`project` set — no real Sentry project exists yet (out of scope for this change, same rule as `eas init`/EAS Updates below). Without them the plugin falls back to SENTRY_ORG/SENTRY_PROJECT env vars at native-build time, which also aren't set, so this stays inert. It only affects native source-map upload config, not JS runtime behavior — see src/lib/sentry.ts for the runtime guard.

widgets.name: TodayWidget
widgets.label: GoalSlot — Today
widgets.description: Your next scheduled block, or today's progress. Tap to open the app.

extra._messagingComment: Origin of the jiffy-messaging deployment. Null = messaging is off in this build: the Messages screens stay unregistered, the drawer entry is hidden, and no socket or token request is ever made. Override per environment with EXPO_PUBLIC_MESSAGING_URL / EXPO_PUBLIC_MESSAGING_WS_URL — app.config.js layers those on top of these, and derives the ws:// URL from the http:// one when only the latter is set.

updates._comment: NON-FUNCTIONAL PLACEHOLDER. `url` needs a real EAS project ID, which only exists after running `eas init`/`eas update:configure` against an Expo account — explicitly out of scope for this change. `enabled: false` keeps expo-updates from trying to check this placeholder URL at runtime (it would otherwise fail every launch). Flip `enabled` to true and swap in the real https://u.expo.dev/<project-id> URL once EAS is set up.
